entries.name: Customs and Excise Duties
entries.note: Section 90 gave the Commonwealth exclusive power over customs and excise; a uniform federal tariff was legislated in the Customs Tariff Act 1902.

entries.name: Bank Notes Tax
entries.note: A ten per cent annual tax on private bank note issues effectively ended private note issue in Australia.

entries.name: Federal Land Tax
entries.note: The Land Tax Act 1910 imposed a progressive tax on the unimproved capital value of land above an exemption threshold.

entries.name: Federal Estate Duty
entries.note: The Estate Duty Assessment Act 1914 imposed Commonwealth duty on deceased estates to fund the First World War.

entries.name: Federal Income Tax
entries.note: The Income Tax Assessment Act 1915 created a Commonwealth income tax operating alongside existing state income taxes.

entries.name: Entertainments Tax
entries.note: The Entertainments Tax Assessment Act 1916 taxed payments for admission to cinemas, theatres and sporting events.

entries.name: War-time Profits Tax
entries.note: The War-time Profits Tax Assessment Act 1917 taxed business profits above a pre-war standard rate of return.

entries.name: Wholesale Sales Tax
entries.note: A single-stage tax on the wholesale value of goods was introduced to replace Depression-reduced customs revenue.

entries.name: War-time Company Tax
entries.note: The War-time (Company) Tax Act 1940 taxed company profits exceeding five per cent of capital employed.

entries.name: Gift Duty
entries.note: The Gift Duty Act 1941, assented 29 October 1941, taxed inter vivos gifts to protect the estate duty base.

entries.name: Payroll Tax
entries.note: A Commonwealth payroll tax of 2.5 per cent commenced 1 July 1941 to finance child endowment payments.

entries.name: Uniform Income Tax
entries.note: Wartime legislation gave the Commonwealth sole occupancy of the income tax field, with grants paid to states that withdrew.

entries.name: War-time Company Tax
entries.note: The wartime company tax and war-time profits arrangements were discontinued after the Second World War ended.

entries.name: Federal Land Tax
entries.note: The Land Tax Abolition Act 1952 ended Commonwealth land tax, leaving the field to the states.

entries.name: Entertainments Tax
entries.note: The Entertainments Tax Abolition Act 1953 repealed the Commonwealth entertainments tax from 1 October 1953.

entries.name: Payroll Tax
entries.note: The Pay-roll Tax (Termination of Commonwealth Tax) Act 1971 transferred payroll tax to the states from 1 September 1971.

entries.name: Crude Oil Production Levy
entries.note: The 1975-76 Budget imposed a levy of two dollars per barrel on Australian-produced crude oil.

entries.name: Departure Tax
entries.note: A ten dollar departure tax commenced in October 1978 to recover passenger processing costs at air and sea ports.

entries.name: Federal Estate Duty
entries.note: Commonwealth estate duty ceased to apply to deaths occurring on or after 1 July 1979.

entries.name: Gift Duty
entries.note: Commonwealth gift duty was abolished at the same time as estate duty, from 1 July 1979.

entries.name: Medicare Levy
entries.note: The Medicare Levy Act 1984 imposed a levy of one per cent of taxable income from February 1984.

entries.name: Capital Gains Tax
entries.note: Real capital gains on assets acquired after 19 September 1985 became assessable income.

entries.name: Fringe Benefits Tax
entries.note: The Fringe Benefits Tax Act 1986 taxed employers on the value of non-cash benefits provided to employees.

entries.name: Medicare Levy rate increase to 1.25 per cent
entries.note: The levy rose from 1 per cent to 1.25 per cent in December 1986 to offset rising medical costs.

entries.name: Dividend Imputation
entries.note: Imputation credits replaced classical company taxation, removing double taxation of Australian company profits distributed to resident shareholders.

entries.name: Petroleum Resource Rent Tax
entries.note: A profits-based tax on offshore petroleum projects other than the North West Shelf, at 40 per cent of taxable profit.

entries.name: Superannuation Guarantee Levy
entries.note: The Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992 required employers to make minimum superannuation contributions or pay a charge.

entries.name: Medicare Levy rate increase to 1.4 per cent
entries.note: The levy rose to 1.4 per cent of taxable income from July 1993 to fund additional health outlays.

entries.name: Departure Tax
entries.note: The 1978 departure tax was replaced by the passenger movement charge from July 1995.

entries.name: Medicare Levy rate increase to 1.5 per cent
entries.note: The levy rose to 1.5 per cent from July 1995 and remained at that rate until 2014.

entries.name: Passenger Movement Charge
entries.note: The charge replaced the departure tax in July 1995, initially set at 27 dollars per departing passenger.

entries.name: Medicare Levy Surcharge
entries.note: From 1 July 1997 higher-income earners without private hospital cover paid an additional one per cent surcharge.

entries.name: Superannuation Contributions Surcharge
entries.note: A surcharge on employer superannuation contributions for higher-income earners applied to contributions made after 20 August 1996.

entries.name: Goods and Services Tax
entries.note: A 10 per cent broad-based consumption tax commenced 1 July 2000 under A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999.

entries.name: Luxury Car Tax
entries.note: A 25 per cent tax applied to the GST-inclusive value of cars above a set threshold from 1 July 2000.

entries.name: Wholesale Sales Tax
entries.note: The wholesale sales tax was repealed from 1 July 2000 when the GST commenced.

entries.name: Wine Equalisation Tax
entries.note: A 29 per cent tax on the wholesale value of wine commenced with the GST on 1 July 2000.

entries.name: Financial Institutions Duty
entries.note: States abolished the duty from 1 July 2001 under the Intergovernmental Agreement accompanying the GST.

entries.name: Fuel excise indexation
entries.note: Half-yearly indexation of petrol and diesel excise to the consumer price index was ended in March 2001.

entries.name: Bank Account Debits Tax
entries.note: The state debits tax was removed by 1 July 2005 under the GST intergovernmental agreement.

entries.name: Superannuation Contributions Surcharge
entries.note: The surcharge did not apply to superannuation contributions made on or after 1 July 2005.

entries.name: Temporary Flood and Cyclone Reconstruction Levy
entries.note: A one-year income tax levy of 0.5 and 1.0 per cent applied above 50,000 and 100,000 dollars in 2011-12.

entries.name: Carbon Pricing Mechanism
entries.note: The Clean Energy Act 2011 imposed a fixed carbon price of 23 dollars per tonne on liable emitters from 1 July 2012.

entries.name: Minerals Resource Rent Tax
entries.note: From 1 July 2012 a 30 per cent tax applied to above-normal profits from iron ore and coal extraction.

entries.name: Temporary Flood and Cyclone Reconstruction Levy
entries.note: The levy was legislated for the 2011-12 income year only and ceased on 30 June 2012.

entries.name: Carbon Pricing Mechanism
entries.note: The Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Act 2014 repealed carbon pricing with effect from 1 July 2014.

entries.name: Fuel excise indexation
entries.note: Half-yearly indexation of fuel excise to the consumer price index was reinstated from November 2014.

entries.name: Medicare Levy rate increase to 2 per cent
entries.note: The levy rose from 1.5 to 2 per cent from 1 July 2014 to help fund the National Disability Insurance Scheme.

entries.name: Minerals Resource Rent Tax
entries.note: The Minerals Resource Rent Tax Repeal and Other Measures Act 2014 removed the tax from 30 September 2014.

entries.name: Temporary Budget Repair Levy
entries.note: A two per cent levy applied to individual taxable income above 180,000 dollars for the 2014-15 to 2016-17 years.

entries.name: Diverted Profits Tax
entries.note: A 40 per cent tax on profits diverted offshore by significant global entities applied to income years starting on or after 1 July 2017.

entries.name: Major Bank Levy
entries.note: A levy of 0.015 per cent per quarter applied to liabilities of authorised deposit-taking institutions above a threshold from 1 July 2017.

entries.name: Temporary Budget Repair Levy
entries.note: The levy was legislated for three years and ceased to apply after 30 June 2017.

gaps: No division or voting data yet. Both public Hansard mirrors need an API key.
No debt, receipts or spending figures yet. Those sit in Budget spreadsheets rather than an API, and are the next thing to land.
Federal only. No state parliaments, no local councils.
The tax timeline is compiled by hand, so it can be incomplete. Every entry links to its source so you can check it, and corrections are public.
method: Each entry is a distinct Commonwealth tax being created or ended, sourced to a Treasury, Parliamentary Library, ATO or legislation.gov.au record.
Rate changes are listed but marked, and do not move the running count. Putting the Medicare levy up is not a new tax.
Two state taxes abolished under the GST agreement are listed for completeness and marked, because the Commonwealth did not levy them.
A tax handed to the states is recorded as abolished federally. The tax did not disappear; the level of government collecting it changed.
The party shown is the party in office at the time, under the name then current.
This does not track thresholds, brackets or bracket creep, which move the tax burden without adding or removing a tax.
